text:
Oncall Bot: PAGER: [HIGH] Suspicious auth traffic — auth-service error rate spike + repeated 401s from 52.14.32.0/24. Possible leaked token or credentials. AlertID: ALT-2026-1123. Escalation to oncall.
Alex Chen: ack. paging @Jordan (SRE oncall). I'll stand by.
Jordan (SRE): I'm on it. first checks: tailing auth-service logs, checking WAF, confirming blast radius. tagging security.
Maria Gómez (Security): thx. preserve evidence: do not delete logs or indices. snapshot the affected ES index to s3 and restrict write access. also capture current IAM/role assignments.
Lee Park (EngOps): pulling logs now. running quick grep:
```
$ jq -r '.message' /var/log/auth-service/requests.log | grep -E "(Authorization:|api_key|token)" | head -n 20
"[2026-03-10T21:10:02Z] POST /v1/auth token=redacted"
"[2026-03-10T21:10:02Z] 401 /v1/auth from 52.14.32.18"
"[2026-03-10T21:10:03Z] 401 /v1/auth from 52.14.32.19"
```
Looks like repeated 401/403s and some successful 200s from same prefix.
Jordan (SRE): any successful sessions with elevated scope? check token introspection logs for suspicious scopes.
Lee Park (EngOps): running token-introspect search across logs. sample from introspect service:
```
{"ts":"2026-03-10T21:09:58Z","token_id":"t_9X...","scope":"service:full_write","client_ip":"52.14.32.18"}
```
That's bad — token had full_write scope.
Maria Gómez (Security): do NOT rotate keys before we snapshot evidence. We need chain-of-custody. If creds leaked, rotate, but after forensics captures initial state. Prepare rotation plan now.
Alex Chen: understood. Jordan, can we put auth-service behind temporary stricter ACLs (denylist 52.14.32.0/24) while we investigate? will that break customers?
Jordan (SRE): we can add IP denylist at edge for that prefix. Risk: if NATs overlap with customer IPs could cause impact. Raj, any customers on that prefix?
Raj Patel (CS): checking customer IPs. one enterprise customer does use a cloud provider that could overlap, but their IPs are in a different range. I'll ping account team for the top 10 customers with errors.
Lee Park (EngOps): applied temporary deny rule in WAF for 52.14.32.0/24 — monitoring for 5m.
Deploy Bot: WAF rule add succeeded (rule-id: waf-rot-17611). Propagation ~20s.
Jordan (SRE): 2m after denylist: error spike down 70%, successful auths from that prefix stopped. good containment.
Maria Gómez (Security): snapshot taken: es://auth-logs-2026-03-10-17611 -> s3://forensics-snapshots/ALT-2026-1123.tar.gz. Access restricted, checksum recorded. next: enumerate service principals that could have issued tokens.
Lee Park (EngOps): listing service accounts with token issuance rights:
```
$ gcloud iam service-accounts list --project=redwood-prod --format=json
["svc-auth-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com", "svc-ingest@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"]
```
Jordan (SRE): plan: 1) preserve evidence (done), 2) rotate keys/tokens for affected principals, 3) force short-lived token invalidation on runtime, 4) run search for leaked secrets in logs and indexes, 5) communicate to customers if impacted.
Maria Gómez (Security): agreed. I'll own the forensics and escalation to legal/compliance if we confirm exfil.
Alex Chen: action items then: Lee to prepare rotation scripts, Jordan to coordinate runtime invalidation, Raj to prepare external comms, Maria to lead forensics, Alex to coordinate exec notification.
Lee Park (EngOps): draft rotation plan (commands below) — will wait for sign-off before executing:
```
# rotate GCP service account keys
$ gcloud iam service-accounts keys create new-key.json --iam-account=svc-auth-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# upload to KMS/HSM and revoke old key
$ gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=prod --key=svc-auth-prod-key --plaintext-file=new-key.json --ciphertext-file=new-key.enc
# revoke
$ gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete old-key-id --iam-account=svc-auth-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
```
Also: rotate internal app tokens and restart auth-service pods to ensure cached tokens drop.
Jordan (SRE): for runtime invalidation, we'll bump token version in config and trigger rolling restart of auth and gateway:
```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/auth-service TOKEN_VERSION=v2
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deploy/gateway
```
Maria Gómez (Security): we need to rotate any long-lived tokens embedded in logs or configs. Search ES indices for patterns (api_key=, token=, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, etc.). Coordinate with Data team to scrub / redact after evidence capture.
Raj Patel (CS): drafted customer advisory (internal):
"We identified suspicious traffic affecting authentication endpoints. We've contained the activity and are rotating credentials. Some customers may have experienced auth errors between 21:08 and 21:20 UTC. We will notify affected customers within 2 hours once we've confirmed impact. — Raj/CS"
Alex Chen: good. Maria, do we communicate to customers now or wait until we confirm tokens were exposed?
Maria Gómez (Security): wait for initial impact list from Jordan & Lee. If confirmed leaked credentials tied to customer accounts, we must notify immediately per policy. Otherwise send precautionary advisory.
Lee Park (EngOps): I'm seeing a handful of tokens that succeeded with full_write. correlating token_id -> service_account -> creation_time: one key created 2026-02-02 for svc-auth-prod. Could be the culprit.
Jordan (SRE): recommendation: rotate svc-auth-prod keys now after snapshot. We have forensic snapshot. I vote rotate now and invalidate tokens (we can force block by token version bump). Any objections?
Alex Chen: no objections from me. Maria?
Maria Gómez (Security): rotate now. we've captured evidence and locked writes to index. proceed.
Lee Park (EngOps): executing key rotation now. posting commands and output:
```
2026-03-10T21:35:12Z gcloud iam service-accounts keys create /tmp/new-svc-auth-key.json --iam-account=svc-auth-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com
2026-03-10T21:36:02Z Uploaded key to KMS prod keyring.
2026-03-10T21:36:10Z Deleted old key old-key-id
```
Deploy Bot: Secret update applied to secretstore (secret: svc-auth-prod-creds) — version v3.
Jordan (SRE): bumping TOKEN_VERSION and restarting auth/gateway now; rolling restart in progress.
Deploy Bot: rollout status: auth-service: 3/3 updated, gateway: 5/5 updated.
Jordan (SRE): runtime token invalidation complete. monitoring for anomalous auths.
Lee Park (EngOps): running wide grep for plaintext keys in logs and ES indices. found entries referencing 'svc-auth-prod-key' in an archived S3 log (ingest pipeline). marking for redaction and adding incident tag.
Maria Gómez (Security): escalate to Legal & Compliance: possible credentials exposure. sending case details.
Raj Patel (CS): quick update from support: one major customer reported auth failures ~21:12; their integration uses service account tokens for server-to-server calls. I'm preparing a targeted notification.
Alex Chen: Status: containment and mitigation actions performed: denylist applied, snapshot taken, keys rotated, runtime invalidation deployed. Impact: transient auth failures for some customers; likely resolved for new tokens. next: confirm whether tokens were exfiltrated and if customer credentials were directly leaked.
Jordan (SRE): still seeing a small number of 401s from new IPs, investigating whether attacker switched IPs. added more rate-limiting and geo-blocks for suspect patterns.
Maria Gómez (Security): start forensic timeline, gather who had access to the old key, grep audit logs for key download events, check CI systems for accidental key commit.
Lee Park (EngOps): searching repo commits for leaked key material: running git-secrets scan across prod repos.
```
$ git-secrets --scan
No matches found in primary repos.
```
Maria Gómez (Security): good. possible cause: exfil from a compromised ephemeral host or third-party contractor. We'll need to validate ingress logs and S3 access logs.
Jordan (SRE): handoff: I'm going offline in 20m. Maria will lead the long-running investigation. tagging follow-up checklist in ops board.
Alex Chen: Jordan — thanks for handling the immediate containment. Maria — you'll coordinate forensics and final customer comms. Raj — prepare a customer-facing advisory draft; include timeframe and mitigation steps.
Raj Patel (CS): draft prepared — will post to #customer-bulletins for review in 30m. suggests offering token rotation guidance for customers and recommended credential best practices.
Maria Gómez (Security): open ticket in Jira: ALT-2026-1123-INV — assign to security, eng-ops, and sre. also schedule incident bridge for 10:00 UTC tomorrow to review full scope and next steps.
Alex Chen: setting incident severity to Sev2 for now. we'll escalate if we confirm widespread data exposure.
Jordan (SRE): final note before handoff: all active older keys for svc-auth-prod are revoked, WAF denylist is in place, rolling restarts done. monitoring dashboard: auth error rate back to baseline. I'll update the oncall log and add runbook pointers.
Oncall Bot: Incident ALT-2026-1123 updated: state=mitigating, assignees=[Maria Gómez (Security), Lee Park (EngOps), Raj Patel (CS)]. Next update expected in 1h.
Alex Chen: thanks everyone. staying on this channel for the next updates. please add any suspicious findings to the Jira and the forensics S3 path.
